title: Press a game case's hub to free the disc, then stand the disc upright and slide it into a slot-loading console
instruction: Take the game disc out of its case and put it into the console.
context: Loading a game or film disc is an everyday task in homes with consoles and players. A game case holds its disc on a hub with spring teeth: the disc comes off only while the hub's centre button is pressed, and lifting it otherwise just lifts the case (and can crack a real disc), so one hand presses while the other lifts. The disc is wider than the gripper opens and 1.2 mm thick, so it is held by its edge and turned upright on the way, and a 5 mm slot leaves under 2 mm either side. No disc, case or console task is on the board.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Layout A is given first, layout B in brackets. Console: a black games console with white side panels (10.4 cm wide, 26 cm deep, 30 cm tall), standing upright, fixed, its front face at x 47 facing the arms, centred at y 6. Its slot-loading drive's slot is vertical in the front face: 5 mm wide and 13.2 cm tall, its middle 10 cm above the table, behind a flared mouth 12 mm wide narrowing to 5 mm over 8 mm; the drive bay behind it is 13.5 cm deep. Storage box: a brown box 8.5 cm tall under the case. Game case: a blue plastic game case (tray half 13.5 x 17.1 cm, 70 g) lying open on the box, the cover half (with an orange insert) on +y; the hub at x 43, y 21 [B: x 42, y 22]. A thumb cut-out 44 mm wide and 32 mm deep in the tray's near edge (toward the arms) overhangs the box. The hub: a seat ring 34 mm across, a post through the disc's hole, three spring teeth over the hole's edge, and a centre button 12 mm across that stands 7 mm proud and presses 2.5 mm (600 N/m); the teeth draw in while it is pressed 1.5 mm or more. Disc: a 120 mm disc, 1.2 mm thick, 15 mm hole, 16 g, blue label up, on the hub. Both arms start in the raised ready pose with their grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a ruler. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the disc touches the table outside the console (dropped). Otherwise 1.0 once the drive has taken the disc: it went in upright (within 10 degrees of square to the slot), centred (within 2.5 mm across the slot and 12 mm up or down) and 7 cm deep, and the drive drew it in. 0.5 if the disc went at least 2 cm into the slot. 0.25 if it came off the hub (its centre 1 cm or more from its place on the hub). Else 0.
reset_notes: Eject the disc, put it back on the case's hub label up and press it home, and lay the case open on its box with the thumb cut-out toward the arms. Use a scratched spare disc for trials.
fidelity: Disc and case are rigid with real dimensions; the hub's teeth are three blocks on radial slides that the task file draws in while the sprung button is pressed. The console's drive is not modelled mechanically: once the disc is 7 cm in, upright and centred, the task file draws it in and holds it. The console is fixed. Scratches and fingerprints are not judged.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (arms stayed near their bases; never reached the case); demo: 1.0 (disc drawn into the console at step 475)
